To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the nucleonstructure is modified in nuclei, (2) the modifications are determined by the nuclear forces, and (3) the modifications are small and can be studied in detail by deep-inelastic lepton scattering on nuclear targets.

the nucleon structure in light nuclei is modified by the nuclear forces in such a way that the pattern of the modifications is completely different from that of heavy nuclei and that the modifications evolve as a function of the atomic number A in a two-stage manner.
(i) the EMC effect is a manifestation of the evolution of the nucleons structure in the field of nuclear forces and that (ii) the nucleon-structure modifications evolve in a two-stage manner.

a relativistic field-theoretic approach to the problem of the nucleon structure in nuclear matter.
the study of nucleon structure and its modification in the nuclear field in a unified approach.
the development of a new relativistic field-theoretic approach to the problem of the evolution of the nucleons structure with A.

the EMC effect is a manifestation of the modification of the nucleons in the field of nuclear forces.

the relativistic theory of nuclear structure functions developed here is in good agreement with the experimental data and allows the interpretation of the experimental results on the evolution of the nucleons in light and heavy nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relativistic theory of the nucleon-structure evolution is a new and powerful tool for the study of the nuclear many-body problem and the structure of nucleons in the nucleus.
we have obtained the first consistent relativistic theory of the modifications of nucleonstructure in very light nuclei and that the results are in good agreement with the experimental data.
we have obtained a new approach to the relativistic theory of the structure of nucleons in nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the EMC effect in light nuclei can be described within a single theoretical approach, in contrast with the situation in the case of heavy nuclei, where the EMC effect can only be studied within a phenomenological approach.
the nucleon-structure evolution as a function of the nuclear mass number A is a universal phenomenon.
the relativistic approach to studying lepto- and electrodisintegration of very light nuclei makes it possible to obtain a unified picture of the evolution of the nucleonic structure in nuclei.
